title: Nondeterminism versus determinism with two two-way heads
formal: Is there a finite alphabet Sigma and a language L⊆Sigma* recognized by a nondeterministic two-way two-head finite automaton but by no deterministic two-way two-head finite automaton, under the nonsensing model below?
definitions:
The input tape is read-only and contains a left endmarker, the finite input, and a right endmarker. A machine has finitely many states and two labelled heads. Initially both heads scan the first input symbol, or the right endmarker for empty input. A transition depends only on the current state and the ordered pair of scanned symbols; it chooses a new state and, for each head, a movement in {−1,0,1}. Heads cannot move outside the endmarkers. There is no extra predicate testing whether the heads occupy the same position: seeing identical symbols does not reveal coincidence.

A run accepts if it is finite and halts in an accepting state with no enabled transition. A word is accepted by a nondeterministic machine when at least one run accepts. Other runs may reject or continue forever. A deterministic machine has at most one transition per state and scanned-symbol pair; it need not halt on words outside its language. The finite control may be arbitrarily large but is fixed independently of input length. Neither machine has a work tape, counter, stack, advice or extra head. The question compares language classes, not state-size blowups for simulating a specific machine.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked language separation, including a nondeterministic recognizer and a proof excluding every deterministic two-head recognizer, or prove equality of these two language classes in Lean. A simulation using more heads or a separation only for one-way input is insufficient.
context:
Holzer, Kutrib and Malcher define the standard multihead model using scanned symbols and independently moving heads. Their survey connects unrestricted numbers of heads to logarithmic-space complexity.

The present question keeps the number of heads exactly two on both sides. Statements about unions over all head counts do not by themselves answer that fixed-resource comparison.
why: This isolates the power of nondeterminism at a fixed number of heads, rather than the state cost of simulation.

import_provenance.original_title: Does nondeterminism add power with two two-way heads?
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a language recognized by a nondeterministic two-way finite automaton with two input heads that no deterministic two-way finite automaton with two heads recognizes? This asks about recognition power with unrestricted finite control, rather than the number of states needed for a simulation.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The equality of these two language classes would imply L=NL; the known strict hierarchy obtained by adding more heads does not settle this comparison.

sentences: Two read-only heads move in both directions on a marked input tape.
Nondeterministic control can choose among enabled transitions.
The target asks whether that choice recognizes a language unavailable to deterministic control with the same two heads.
Heads cannot directly sense that they coincide.
Acceptance permits nonterminating rejecting runs and does not impose a state-size bound.
